A Purity Beans jar costs between ₹209 and ₹908 depending on the blend and size. In a Mumbai high-rise, the kettle clicks off at 6:47 a.m. while the balcony door slides open to let in humid air and distant horns. My neighbor, a chartered accountant who swears by single-origin pour-overs on weekends, still keeps a jar of instant beside the sink for weekday mornings. He spoons a heaping teaspoon into his favorite chipped mug, pours water just off the boil, and stirs exactly seven times — a ritual he claims "wakes the granules up." Down the lane in a Bangalore co-living space, a designer froths cold milk with a ₹300 handheld whisk, crowns her Ultra Blend with a dusting of cocoa, and calls it her "cafe mocha hack." A Delhi professor, meanwhile, dissolves Purica in a splash of hot water, tops it with chilled oat milk, and swears the caramel notes survive the shortcut. Standing in the aisle or scrolling late at night, the decision usually comes down to what you actually drink. Purista (freeze-dried Robusta) sits at ₹319 for 50g and ₹509 for 100g — bold yet smooth with a rich crema. A simple rule: match the jar to the ritual.
